summary: KhetSurvey should be a monolith in BLR1 (Bangalore). Client: Expo (React Native). Server: FastAPI. Data: PostgreSQL (DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL in BLR1 (Bangalore)). Host: DigitalOcean App Platform in BLR1 (Bangalore).

frontend.justification: KhetSurvey is an other on android. Twelve month target 2,000 users, peak 200, MVP 10 weeks, 2 mixed engineers. One TypeScript codebase for Android and iOS, with expo-sqlite for offline rows. Team languages: javascript, python. offline_support is true, so the client keeps its own queue. The description calls out weak phones, so a heavier toolkit had to earn its place.

alternatives.why_not: Kotlin and Jetpack Compose needs kotlin, and this team does not list them.
Flutter needs dart, and this team does not list them.

tradeoffs: On a 2 GB phone the JS runtime is heavier than Kotlin. Ship a release build and keep screens dull.
Store review and native modules still need a real device lab.

backend.justification: A typed Python API. Quick to build, and a natural home for a sync or scoring endpoint. Peak 200, workload write_heavy, realtime off.

alternatives.why_not: NestJS is a weaker match for an other with these priorities. The decorator style is more framework than Fastify, which is fine at three people and noisy at one.
Django is a weaker match for an other with these priorities. Live sockets are not the happy path. A realtime-heavy product wants a different core.

tradeoffs: You assemble auth, migrations, and admin yourself. Django has those, FastAPI does not.

database.justification: Relational, ACID, and available as a managed service in Mumbai, the EU, and the US. The default for money, bookings, and tenancy. Placement follows the host pin: BLR1 (Bangalore).

alternatives.why_not: MySQL is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
MongoDB is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 100 USD.

tradeoffs: A single small node will not meet 99.99 on its own. You pay for a standby.
Very large analytical scans want a column store beside it, not instead of it, once you pass a few terabytes.

hosting.justification: cloud_preference is any, deployment_model is managed_cloud, data_residency resolves to india. The pin is BLR1 (Bangalore). A small PaaS with a Bangalore region (BLR1), managed Postgres, and Spaces. The bill is readable. team.has_devops is false, so a host with a small control surface beats a cluster.

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 100 USD.
Google Cloud Run is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 100 USD.

tradeoffs: Past a few thousand concurrent sockets you want a hyperscaler.
Fewer compliance attestations than AWS or Azure.

supporting.justification: Phone OTP for users in India should use a domestic SMS route (DLT-registered). MSG91 is that route. Store only a hash of the code, in the India database.

alternatives.why_not: It works, and it is a worse fit for the residency of the phone numbers.
The user record would sit in a Google project whose region story is easy to get wrong, and phone-auth pricing surprises small budgets.

tradeoffs: SMS cost scales with logins, not with servers. A noisy retry loop will blow the budget before the database does.

supporting.justification: Uploads have to live somewhere durable. The bucket is private. The app issues short-lived URLs. KYC, health, or customer files do not sit on a public CDN.

alternatives.why_not: A second file system splits retention and access reviews. One bucket next to the app is enough.

tradeoffs: Lifecycle rules are part of the design. Nobody deletes old uploads unless you ask the bucket to.

supporting.justification: A short pipeline: test, then deploy with short-lived cloud credentials. Keep production secrets out of the repo.

alternatives.why_not: It is a fine CI. It is also a second account this team has not said they already run.

tradeoffs: A green pipeline is not a test plan. Someone still has to write the tests.

supporting.choice: SQLite on the device, with an outbound sync queue
supporting.justification: offline_support is true. The phone keeps survey or job rows locally and posts them when the network returns. SQLite is the maintained on-device store. Compress photos before they join the queue.

alternatives.choice: MongoDB Realm and Atlas Device Sync
alternatives.why_not: Atlas Device Sync and the Realm SDKs were removed on 30 September 2025. A new app should not start there.

tradeoffs: Conflicts are your code. Last-write-wins is a product decision, not a database feature.

assumptions: Compute (do_app, small band) about 12 to 50 USD.
PostgreSQL (do, small band) about 15 to 31 USD.
DigitalOcean Spaces is about 5 USD per month and includes 250 GiB.
SMS OTP is usage priced. The band assumes a fraction of users request a code each month, about 0.004 USD per active user, and ignores promotional SMS.
CI minutes are assumed inside the free tier for this team size.
Scale band is small: 2000 users at 12 months, peak 200, 100.0 GB stored.
This is an order-of-magnitude band, not an invoice. Taxes, support plans, and human time are excluded.

warnings.message: The network in the description is weak. Downscale photos on the device (1280 px on the long edge is enough) before they join the upload queue.
The description mentions low-RAM phones. Ship a release build, keep the screen count small, and test on a 2 GB device. A debug build is not the test.
OTP SMS is usage priced and can pass the infra budget on its own. Cap retries, and watch the SMS bill as a separate line.
DPDP applies. You still need a lawful purpose, a consent or legitimate-use record, a retention period, and a way for a person to access or erase their data. The region pin is not the whole duty.
GPS points are personal data. Store the consent flag on the same row and set a retention period.
Microservices and Kubernetes were not chosen. The team is 2 and the 12 month user count is 2,000. A single deployable is the design until those numbers move.

assumptions: budget.existing_licences defaulted to an empty list.
scale.geographic_spread defaulted to national because data_residency is india.
data.sensitivity defaulted to confidential because a privacy law is set.
requirements.expected_rps_peak was not set. Capacity uses peak concurrency (200), which is roughly 20 requests per second if about one in ten connected users acts at once.
